note: Cat and animal volunteer work around Seattle for Sheila (9): what she can do now, with an adult where the source says so, and what opens at 13 or 16 so she can look ahead. Every item names its source URL and the date it was checked; confirm details on the page before signing up. Never add a fact without a source.

forms.name: Community Service Hours Log
forms.note: Seattle Humane's official monthly log: one row per session with date, time in, description of activity, time out, total time, and a signature. The Reports page prints this format filled in from the tracker; take it along for the signature.

raskc.name: Regional Animal Services of King County

contact.address: Kent Pet Adoption Center, 21615 64th Ave S, Kent, WA
14717 Aurora Ave N, Shoreline, WA 98133 (per the contact page; confirm the current location before visiting)

items.title: No-sew cat blankets
items.summary: Make small fleece blankets for the cats waiting to be adopted.
details: All the cats in Seattle Humane's care receive a blanket or towel to make their cubby more comfortable; most of the time a cat's special blanket goes home with them when they are adopted.
Blankets around 18 × 20 inches are suggested for cats.
Written and video instructions for making no-sew blankets are on the project page.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated on the page.

items.commitment: One sitting per batch; drop off when you have a few.
items.location: At home; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Follow the no-sew instructions on the project page, then bring the blankets to the shelter. Contact Education Services for drop-off details.

items.title: Homemade cat toys from recycled objects
items.summary: Turn old socks and paper tubes into catnip toys for shelter cats.
details: Old socks become catnip toys when stuffed with scrap paper, toilet paper tubes, or other crinkly items with catnip.
The project page lists more ways to make cat toys from recycled or reusable objects.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated on the page.

items.location: At home; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Make the toys following the project page, then bring them to the shelter with any blankets.

items.title: Pet food drive
items.summary: Organize a pet food drive in the neighborhood or at school.
details: Donations of pet food, supplies and toys are always appreciated.
Items are distributed through Oogie's Ohana Pet Food Bank at Seattle Humane, which helps provide 1 million meals each year to pets in the community.
Youth can help pets and earn school service hours by donating, fundraising or supporting the pet food bank.
Community service hours are recorded on Seattle Humane's monthly Community Service Hours Log, one row per session with time in, time out and a signature (form linked on the organization).

ages.note: No age limit stated; collecting from neighbors and delivering needs an adult.

items.commitment: A few weeks of collecting, then one delivery.
items.location: Neighborhood or school; deliver to Seattle Humane
items.howTo: Pick a collection window, tell neighbors or the class what to bring, then deliver the donations to the shelter. Email Education Services for current needs.

items.title: Shelter Helper at the Kent shelter (from age 9 with a parent)
items.summary: Real shelter chores for kids as young as nine, alongside a parent or guardian.
details: RASKC offers volunteer opportunities for ages 16 and 17 with guardian consent, and ages 9–15 with an accompanying guardian.
The Shelter Helper role is available for ages 9+; youth 9–15 must be accompanied by their parent or legal guardian.
Listed Shelter Helper shifts involve washing dishes and doing laundry at the Kent Pet Adoption Center; training is provided for all volunteer roles.
Register for a volunteer orientation to start; questions go to RASKC.Volunteers@kingcounty.gov.

ages.note: From age 9 with a parent or guardian; 16–17 with consent.

items.commitment: Scheduled shifts, typically an hour or two.
items.location: Kent Pet Adoption Center, 21615 64th Ave S, Kent
items.howTo: Register for a RASKC volunteer orientation from the volunteer page, then sign up for Shelter Helper shifts together.

items.title: Cat cozy blankets and other group projects for RASKC
items.summary: Make cozy blankets for the shelter cats, or run a fundraiser or poster project as a family.
details: RASKC's group volunteering options include making cat cozy blankets, organizing fundraisers, putting up posters in the community, or making YouTube videos.
Children may also take part in caring for animals through the fostering program, with an adult in the household as the official volunteer.

ages.note: Group and family project; no age stated.

items.commitment: One session per batch or project.
items.location: At home; deliver to the Kent shelter
items.howTo: Email RASKC.Volunteers@kingcounty.gov to ask for the current blanket specifications and drop-off arrangements, then make a batch.

items.title: PAWS Preteen Workshops (ages 9–12)
items.summary: Two-hour workshops at the Lynnwood shelter where preteens do service projects for the animals.
details: Dedicated to educating preteens ages 9–12 on how to improve the lives of animals at PAWS and in the community; preteens complete mission-driven work through community service projects while building leadership skills and learning from guest speakers.
Projects include helping with groundwork, creating animal enrichment, supporting shelter operations and more.
Held in person at PAWS in Lynnwood; the summer series ran weekly, Tuesdays 11:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. and Thursdays 2:00–4:00 p.m.
Pricing has been listed as $20 per two-hour workshop and as $175 for a ten-week series in different seasons; check the current listing and ask education@paws.org about the discount code.
items.howTo: Watch the Teen and Preteen Workshops page for the next series and register; email education@paws.org with questions.

items.title: Make cat toys, scratchers and beds for PAWS
items.summary: PAWS lists kid-friendly things to make at home for the shelter's cats and dogs.
details: At PAWS you must be 18 or older to work with or around animals, so at-home projects are how kids help directly.
Ideas from PAWS: snuffle mats, cardboard cat scratchers, dog toys out of old t-shirts or jeans, cat toys out of fabric, feathers and string, and cat beds sewn from used sweaters.
PAWS also suggests being kind to wildlife: fresh water and bird feeders at home, picking up litter that can harm wild animals.

ages.note: No age limit stated; written for kids.

items.location: At home; deliver to PAWS in Lynnwood
items.howTo: Pick a project from the Kids & Teen Opportunities page, make a batch, and contact PAWS about dropping it off.

items.title: Wish-list drive or birthday donations for PAWS
items.summary: Collect supplies from PAWS's wish list, or ask for donations instead of birthday presents.
details: PAWS receives donations from kids who ask for donations to help animals instead of presents for their birthday.
Kids can organize a FUNdraiser, have a gift drive, collect animal supplies, or all three.
Wish-list items can be bought online and shipped directly to PAWS.

ages.note: No age limit stated; collecting and delivering needs an adult.

items.commitment: A few weeks of collecting, then one delivery or shipment.
items.location: Neighborhood or school; ship or deliver to PAWS
items.howTo: Use the PAWS wish list to tell people what to bring, then deliver or ship the items.

items.title: Kid's Volunteer Day at The NOAH Center
items.summary: A hands-on day at the Stanwood shelter: kids follow a plush pet through the shelter journey and meet the real dogs and cats.
details: Youths 8–13 can register for one of NOAH's Kid's Day volunteer opportunities; regular volunteering starts at 14 (14–15 with a parent).
The Kid's Day page describes it as perfect for kids ages 6–10, all ages welcome with adult supervision, and each camper must be accompanied by an adult.

Kids 'adopt' a plush pet and walk it through intake, medical exams and adoption day, with stations like puppy paw painting, bottle-feeding baby animals, scent trails, agility demos and clicker training; snacks and water are provided, pack a lunch.

ages.note: Ages 8–13 per the youth page (6–10 per the event page); an adult comes along.

items.location: The NOAH Center, 31300 Brandstrom Rd, Stanwood
items.howTo: Watch the Kid's Volunteer Day page for the next date and register; check the current cost there.

items.title: Foster kittens or cats as a family (Seattle Area Feline Rescue)
items.summary: The rescue's shelter volunteers must be 16, and it points younger families to fostering.
details: Volunteers in the rescue must be at least 16; for those under the required age, the rescue recommends discussing fostering with your family.
Foster scenarios include litters of kittens too young for adoption, bottle-baby kittens needing round-the-clock care, adult cats who need socialization, and adult cats with other needs.
Kittens come into the adoption center regularly for check-ups, normally 2–4 times a month; homes without regular transportation are welcome for adult cats in longer-term foster.
To start, read the Foster Handbook and fill out the online Foster Information Form.

ages.note: The registered foster is an adult; the child helps at home.

items.howTo: Read the Foster Handbook on the foster page and submit the Foster Information Form.

items.title: Foster Cat Program (Seattle Animal Shelter)
items.summary: The city shelter calls fostering a wonderful family experience; shelter volunteering itself starts at 18.
details: To volunteer at the Seattle Animal Shelter you must be 18 or older; family participation is allowed and encouraged through fostering.

The shelter says fostering can build a foundation of philanthropy in your children, to select a cat that is age-appropriate for them, and to give children guidance, instructions and rules about caring for an orphaned cat.
A Kitten Care class is offered when more kitten fosters are needed.

ages.note: The registered foster is an adult; the child helps at home.

items.location: At home; the shelter is at 2061 15th Ave W, Seattle
items.howTo: Complete the online volunteer profile and select Foster Care Volunteer–Cats.

items.title: Foster with Homeward Pet (families with young children)
items.summary: Homeward Pet names fostering as the way in for families whose children are too young to volunteer at the shelter.
details: Fostering is described as a great way for families to become involved, especially those with children too young to become volunteers at the shelter.
Foster families provide temporary in-home care, from 2-day kennel breaks to a couple of months of quiet surgery rehab; mostly dogs, from energetic puppies to calm seniors.
Fill out the Volunteer Application; you will be invited to the General Orientation.

ages.note: The registered foster is an adult; the child helps at home.

items.commitment: Two days to a couple of months per foster.
items.howTo: Submit the Volunteer Application on homewardpet.org and attend the General Orientation.

items.title: Purrfect Pals cat sanctuary (from age 13, with a parent until 16)
items.summary: The region's first no-kill cat shelter, on five acres in Arlington.
details: At the main sanctuary in Arlington, volunteers must be 13 or older, and anyone under 16 must be with a parent or guardian.
Volunteers organize fundraising events, sew cat blankets, brush cats, pick up donations, maintain sanctuary grounds, take photos of cats, and more.
Ongoing project needs at the sanctuary include gardening and landscaping, maintenance, painting, cleaning and construction.

ages.note: From age 13; under 16 with a parent or guardian.

items.howTo: Email volunteers@purrfectpals.org from the volunteer page when she turns 13.

items.title: Seattle Area Feline Rescue volunteering (from age 16)
items.summary: Cat care and adoption-center roles at the Shoreline rescue once she is 16.
details: Volunteers in the rescue must be at least 16 years old.
Until then the rescue recommends fostering as a family (listed separately).
items.howTo: Apply through the volunteer page at 16.

items.title: Humane Teen Club (ages 13–17)
items.summary: A school-year club for animal-loving teens at Seattle Humane.
details: For teens ages 13–17 to learn about Seattle Humane, explore animal welfare topics and prepare for future volunteer opportunities.
Members meet two Saturdays per month.
items.commitment: Two Saturdays a month during the school year.
items.howTo: Sign up through the Youth Programs page when the school-year session opens.

items.title: High School Service Shifts (grades 9–12)
items.summary: Routine shelter tasks in winter that earn community service hours.
details: For students entering grades 9–12: assist with routine shelter tasks, meet other teens and earn community service hours.
Tasks such as washing food and water bowls, cleaning crates, or packing pet food.
Offered during winter months; students register for shifts in December and January.
items.commitment: Individual shifts in December and January.
items.howTo: Register on the High School Service Shifts page when winter registration opens.

items.title: Humane Service Training Program (ages 16–17)
items.summary: Structured, hands-on learning for older teens exploring animal-care careers.
details: Designed for motivated 16–17-year-olds interested in animal welfare, community service, and career exploration in the field of animal care.
items.commitment: Structured program; see the page for the schedule.
items.howTo: Apply through the Youth Programs page at 16.
